notes: §1985:VI.6.21.4 GR1: 'The data items referenced by identifier-4 and identifier-7 must not have a zero value.' It is a requirement on the content of the BY identifiers at run time, which the program must meet; the 1985 text states no action for a program that breaks it, so what the compiler owes is to take any BY identifier and augment by its current value. ControlFlowBinder.BindVaryingOperand binds identifier-4 / identifier-7 with no test on the item's value (only a zero BY literal is refused, the separate §1985:VI.6.21.3 SR9, in CheckVaryingOperandRules), and ControlFlowEmitter.Augment reads the BY operand at each augment of EmitVarying's levels, at every edition. The witness runs a VARYING ... AFTER nest whose two BY operands are data items holding 1. Probes at --std 85: a negative BY item, a noninteger one and a negative one over an index-name step as their values say; a BY item holding zero is not diagnosed and leaves the variable unchanged at each augment, the loop ending when its condition does (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-85/out/work-slice-19/p8/a.cob), a deterministic outcome where the rule defines none.

next.reason: 1985: "The data items referenced by identifier-4 and identifier-7 must not have a zero value."; 2023: "GR-12 defines the augment value from the BY identifier with no ban on zero; only "The literal in the BY phrase shall not be zero."". 2023 still has BY identifiers, but no candidate requires their value to be nonzero. Only a zero BY literal is barred (SR-6), so the runtime requirement on identifiers is dropped.
